key_insight: Bayesian inference fused with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize perovskite solar-cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk over time.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted durability improvements by identifying where device failure starts, helping engineers prioritize interface passivation and material design.
method: Photoluminescence imaging captures spatially resolved device behavior during aging.
Drift-diffusion simulations translate images into parameter maps for recombination and transport.
Bayesian inference updates those maps over time to separate bulk, hole-contact, and electron-contact degradation.
evidence_signal: The method was applied to fully fabricated cells aged at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight, revealing strongly non-uniform degradation and improved stability with amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and imaging quality, so mis-specified physics or limited observability could affect localization of degradation.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
